newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Moody's says Saudi banks' credit outlook stable.
newsitem.headline: Moody's says Saudi banks' credit outlook stable.

text.p: Moody's Investors Service said on Thursday that the outlook for Saudi Arabian banks' credit quality was generally stable.

The Saudi banking system is generally profitable, liquid and adequately capitalised, and for most banks, asset quality is secure, the credit rating agency said in a statement citing its new report on the Saudi banking system.
Moody's rates seven banks in Saudi Arabia and said the ratings on them were stable.
The outlook for United Saudi Commercial Bank was less certain in view of the 34 percent stake the bank's chairman and associates had acquired in Saudi Cairo Bank in early 1996, Moody's said.
But it added that, if handled correctly, a closer relationship between the two banks could have positive ramifications.
Moody's said the principal threat to Saudi banks lay in the possibility of a deterioration of the macro-economic environment, which would lead to an erosion of asset quality.
But it said it believed the banks' vulnerability to adverse economic conditions has been diminishing as a result of their consistent performance during the 1990s.

The Saudi economy' reliance on crude oil sales revenues made it prone to up and down swings, but the economy's structure was now such that a boom/bust cycle on the scale seen in the 1970s and 1980s could not recur, the agency added.
